Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 47 (*Hatthaniddhunaka*, "Shaking the hand") is a monastic training rule (*sekhiya*) preserved in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text lays down proper monastic decorum concerning meals, specifically ruling against shaking one's hands while eating [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature passages in the dossier concern this Vinaya rule, as all search results match citations of verse 47 of the *Sāṃkhyakārikā*.
According to SuttaCentral, Sekhiya 47 shares extensive parallels across the Vinaya literature of diverse early Buddhist lineages [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, corresponding rules appear in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha, and the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Further parallels are preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan recensions representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Lokottaravāda traditions [SuttaCentral].
